claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child in local authority care for 12 weeks (>8) and does not spend 24+ hours/week at home
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help me assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about your child or children first.

**Could you please tell me:**

1. **How many children are you claiming for?**
2. **What is the age of each child?** (or their date of birth)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm claiming for just one child - my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're claiming for your daughter **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, that's excellent news - children under 16 automatically qualify for the basic eligibility criteria on age grounds. However, I need to check a few more things to ensure full eligibility.

Let me proceed with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 1: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

This is mainly relevant for older children, but I need to check it for completeness. Since Alex is only 8, I assume she's not in paid work - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, she doesn't work at all. She's only 8, so she's just at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 2: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in her own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking if Alex is receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in her own right. Since she's 8 years old, I would expect the answer is no - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in her own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 3: Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old and at school, she's clearly not in any apprenticeship program. However, I need to ask this question for completeness - can you confirm that Alex is not in any apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - she's not in any apprenticeship. She's just 8 and in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 4: Does the claimant (you) meet UK residency requirements?**

There are several ways to meet this requirement. Let me ask you about your situation:

**Do any of the following apply to you:**

1. **You normally live in the UK?** (This is the most common situation)

OR

2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

OR

3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** AND one of the following:
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months?
   - You're actively seeking work (jobseeker)?
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and family financially and are NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?
   - You're studying with sufficient resources to support yourself?
   - You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside?

OR

4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad or in certain qualifying countries?**

Which of these (if any) applies to your situation? If none of these apply, you may not meet the residency requirements.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, the first one applies to me - I normally live in the UK. We live here in England.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's straightforward. Let me proceed to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 5: Are you responsible for Alex?**

The key is that responsibility means either:

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to her upkeep** (e.g., paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc. - at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit payment), OR
3. **You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement** that covers her upkeep

Since Alex is your daughter and you mentioned she's at school in England where you live, I assume you live with her and are responsible for her care - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 6: Is there anyone else claiming (or intending to claim) Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming for her?
- Is another family member claiming for her?
- Has anyone else started a claim for her?

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. If multiple people are claiming, HMRC will need to decide who is the rightful claimant.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me proceed to the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 7: Where is Alex living?**

Is Alex:
- In hospital for treatment?
- In local authority care (children's home, secure unit, etc.)?
- Fostered with a foster family?
- Living normally at home (the typical situation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, she's been in local authority care for a while now - she's been in a children's home for a couple of months.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. That's an important detail. Let me check the specific rules for children in care:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Question 8: Regarding Alex's time in care:**

The rules state that Child Benefit can continue for up to 8 weeks when a child is in care. There's an important exception though:

**Can you tell me:**

1. **How long has Alex been in the children's home?** You mentioned "a couple of months" - is that 8 weeks or less, or longer than 8 weeks?

2. **Does Alex spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you?** (For example, weekends or overnight visits)

These details will determine whether she continues to qualify.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's been there for about 12 weeks now, so that's longer than 8 weeks. And no, she doesn't come home - she's at the children's home full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Unfortunately, based on the information you've provided, this means Alex no longer qualifies for Child Benefit under the current rules.

Let me explain why:

**The Rule:** When a child is in local authority care (like a children's home), Child Benefit can only continue for up to 8 weeks. After that period ends, the child is no longer eligible - **unless** they spend at least 24 hours a week at home with you.

**Your Situation:** 
- Alex has been in the children's home for approximately 12 weeks (longer than the 8-week limit)
- She does not spend any time at home with you during the week

Because both of these conditions apply, unfortunately **Alex is no longer eligible for Child Benefit** at this time.

**However, important points to know:**

1. **If Alex's situation changes**, you could potentially claim again. For example, if:
   - Alex comes home to live with you again, OR
   - She starts spending at least 2 consecutive nights per week at home, OR
   - She spends 7 or more consecutive days at home

2. **You should inform HMRC** about Alex's change in circumstances if you're currently receiving Child Benefit for her, as continuing to claim could result in an overpayment that you'd need to repay.

3. **Further guidance:** You can get more information at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care

Is there anything else you'd like to know about this, or any other children you're claiming for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, that's all - Alex is my only child. Thank you for explaining that to me. I understand now that I'm not eligible because she's been in care for longer than 8 weeks and doesn't come home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're welcome. Now that I have all the information about your situation, let me provide you with the formal eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment:**

**Result: INELIGIBLE**

**For: Alex (age 8)**

---

**Why you're not currently eligible:**

Alex does not qualify for Child Benefit because she has been in local authority care for longer than 8 weeks and does not spend sufficient time at home with you. The rules allow Child Benefit to continue for up to 8 weeks when a child enters care, but this period has now ended in Alex's case.

---

**What you can do:**

- **If Alex's situation changes** and she comes home to live with you, or starts spending at least 2 consecutive nights per week at home, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again
- **Contact HMRC** if you're currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex to report the change in circumstances - it's important to do this to avoid an overpayment

**Useful links:**
- https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit-for-children-in-hospital-or-care
- https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit

I hope this has been helpful. If you have any other questions in the future, feel free to ask!

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old and meets all the basic eligibility criteria: she is under 16, does not work, does not receive benefits in her own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. The claimant meets UK residency requirements (normally lives in the UK), is responsible for Alex (living with her address), and there are no other claimants for Alex. Additionally, Alex does not spend at least 24 hours per week at home with the claimant, which would have been an exception to the 8-week rule. Therefore, Alex is ineligible for Child Benefit under the care duration rules.
